questions.why_it_matters: The range claim and hero pack depend on the actual assortment.

questions.why_it_matters: The core demo must show the real product action, not an invented one.

questions.question: Can the ad call Easy Pour instant coffee?
questions.why_it_matters: A category error would mislead the viewer and damage trust.

questions.why_it_matters: Observed storefront values are not approved commercial claims.

questions.question: May the public logo and product images be used in paid advertising?
questions.why_it_matters: Public availability is not an advertising licence.

questions.why_it_matters: The edit, type placement and end card depend on the placement.

questions.question: What hook, brand and CTA structure fits a 20-second YouTube ad?
questions.why_it_matters: A 20-second ad needs early attention, early brand and a clear direction.

questions.question: Can a real brew be shown honestly in 20 seconds?
questions.why_it_matters: The brand instructions include a steep time longer than the ad.

questions.question: Who is the viewer and what do they already believe?
questions.why_it_matters: The hook and proof depend on the viewer's starting point.

findings.observation: The Mixed Bag page describes a range of single-estate coffees from light to dark: Seethargundu light, Thogarihunkal medium, Attikan medium-dark and Vienna dark. It is sold as a pack of 5 or 10.
findings.interpretation: The Mixed Bag is a variety product, so the film can show a range of roast levels without inventing a new assortment.
findings.proposed_action: Use the Mixed Bag as the hero and show four packs: Mixed Bag, Seethargundu light, Attikan medium-dark and Vienna dark. Say only 'light to dark'.

findings.observation: The brewing instructions say to tear the outer sachet, tear the filter top, anchor the filter over a 180-200 ml cup, pour hot water, wait 20 seconds, repeat 2-3 times, then steep for 2 minutes.
findings.interpretation: The real action is a multi-step brew with a steep that cannot fit in 20 seconds at real speed. A truthful demo needs time compression and a visible disclosure.
findings.proposed_action: Show tear, anchor and pour, then compress the repeated pours and steep with a time-lapse cue and the caption 'Brew sequence compressed'.

findings.observation: The Easy Pour FAQ says it is not powdered instant coffee or a premix, but is as quick and hassle-free to brew.
findings.interpretation: Calling it instant coffee would be a category error. The ad should contrast specialty coffee with the convenience, not the product.
findings.proposed_action: Use 'specialty coffee' and 'no equipment', never 'instant coffee'.
findings.evidence_locator: FAQ: Is this the same as instant coffee?

findings.observation: The Mixed Bag page lists pack of 5 at Rs 300 and pack of 10 at Rs 500. The brief does not approve a price or hero pack size.
findings.interpretation: Price and pack size are observed commercial values. They cannot enter the ready cut without brand approval.
findings.proposed_action: Keep price out of the ready cut and hold the hero pack size for brand confirmation.

findings.observation: The user supplied a Blue Tokai circular logo attachment; the four pack images remain public CDN references. No written paid-media licence or high-resolution pack masters were supplied.
findings.interpretation: The logo file is now a supplied reference, but public availability of the pack images is not an advertising licence. Pack labels are exact commercial elements.
findings.proposed_action: Use the supplied logo; request written paid-media approval and high-resolution masters for the four packs. Hold the pack and logo rights until cleared.

findings.observation: Google recommends 1920x1080 horizontal and 1080x1920 vertical video, and publishes placement-specific safe-zone templates.
findings.interpretation: 16:9 is a valid YouTube master. Exact safe insets must be checked against the chosen placement rather than assumed universal.
findings.proposed_action: Plan a 1920x1080 master with conservative insets and a placement preview before paid media.
findings.evidence_locator: Video ad specs table and safe-zone templates

findings.observation: Google's ABCD guidance asks for early attention, early and repeated branding, focused connection and a clear direction or CTA.
findings.interpretation: A 20-second ad can use a 3-second hook, a 7-second demo, a 5-second range proof and a 5-second close.
findings.proposed_action: Put the pack and brand in the hook, keep the demo single-minded, and land the CTA on the end card.

findings.observation: The brand's brew instructions include a 2-minute steep after pouring. A 20-second film cannot show that at real speed.
findings.interpretation: Time compression is a production treatment, not a product claim. It needs an on-screen disclosure so the demo remains honest.
findings.proposed_action: Use a time-lapse transition and a small 'Brew sequence compressed' disclaimer in the payoff shot.

findings.observation: The brief defines the viewer as busy Indian professionals who already buy cafe or instant coffee and want specialty coffee without equipment.
findings.interpretation: The viewer needs the benefit demonstrated, not a origin lecture. The hook should name the category and show the pack immediately.
findings.proposed_action: Open on 'Specialty coffee' with the pack; use the demo as proof.
findings.evidence_locator: Brief target audience and core message

findings.observation: No finished voice-over, music bed or demonstration footage was supplied.
findings.interpretation: The demo and audio are production requirements with rights and consent gates, not assets already available.
findings.proposed_action: Record the demo, voice and music in Level 2; hold the performer and licence approvals.

findings.observation: The brief names the Mixed Bag, Vienna and Attikan Estate packs and supplies the logo and product-image links. Seethargundu is added from the Mixed Bag page to provide the light endpoint.
findings.interpretation: The exact product set is fixed by the brief, while the creative use of each pack still needs a composition decision.
findings.proposed_action: Use Mixed Bag as hero, Seethargundu, Attikan and Vienna as range support, and keep each label unobstructed.

findings.observation: The brand describes Easy Pour as specialty coffee brewed with hot water in a 180-200 ml cup, with no equipment.
findings.interpretation: The core message is supported by the brand's own instructions, but it is still brand-authored rather than independent product testing.
findings.proposed_action: Use 'no equipment' and 'just a mug and hot water' as brand-supported wording, not a superiority claim.

findings.observation: The supplied hero link points to The Rich & Bold Trio Pack: Vienna, French and Attikan, sold as whole bean or ground coffee, 75 g x 3. It is not Easy Pour and has no built-in filter.
findings.interpretation: The Trio can support the dark end of the range visually, but it cannot replace the Easy Pour hero without changing the core message and demo.
findings.proposed_action: Keep the Easy Pour Mixed Bag as hero; use the Trio page only as a range/pack reference. Do not claim light-to-dark from the dark trio.
findings.evidence_locator: Product title, component list and brewing method

effect_assessments.name: steam_drift
effect_assessments.use_case: Signal fresh coffee and add atmosphere without hiding the pack
effect_assessments.rationale: Steam is a small, physically legible cue that makes the coffee feel hot and fresh without adding a claim.
effect_assessments.feasibility: In-house particle or practical steam; low render cost.
effect_assessments.rights_safety: No third-party media; keep steam clear of the exact label.
effect_assessments.fallback: Static pack plate with a slow grade shift.

effect_assessments.name: macro_pour
effect_assessments.use_case: Show hot water hitting the coffee bed inside the built-in filter
effect_assessments.rationale: The brief asks for the water hitting the grounds; a real macro pour is the clearest proof of the brewing method.
effect_assessments.feasibility: Controlled food shoot at 50 fps, finished at 25 fps.
effect_assessments.rights_safety: Hand model release and food-safe set required.
effect_assessments.fallback: Still pour plate with animated steam and drip.

effect_assessments.name: time_lapse
effect_assessments.use_case: Carry the repeated pours and two-minute steep inside a 20-second film
effect_assessments.rationale: The real brew cannot fit in 20 seconds; a visible time-lapse preserves the method while compressing time honestly.
effect_assessments.rights_safety: Must carry the on-screen disclosure 'Brew sequence compressed'.
effect_assessments.fallback: Short step montage with the same disclosure.

effect_assessments.name: range_fan
effect_assessments.use_case: Show the Mixed Bag plus light, medium-dark and dark packs
effect_assessments.rationale: A four-pack fan makes the light-to-dark range concrete without a catalogue or a second end card.
effect_assessments.feasibility: Product stills with a single camera move.
effect_assessments.rights_safety: All four packs need brand advertising clearance.
effect_assessments.fallback: Captured four-pack still with a slow scale.

effect_assessments.name: finished_steam
effect_assessments.use_case: Show the finished cup as hot, fresh coffee
effect_assessments.rationale: A thin steam plume makes the finished cup read as a real brew rather than a prop.
effect_assessments.feasibility: Practical steam on set or a small particle pass.
effect_assessments.rights_safety: Keep steam clear of the pack label and CTA.
effect_assessments.fallback: Still cup with a simple animated steam plate.

effect_assessments.name: cta_fade
effect_assessments.use_case: Land the purchase prompt after the proof and range
effect_assessments.rationale: A short fade-up gives the CTA its own beat without competing with the product demonstration.
effect_assessments.rights_safety: No added claim; CTA wording remains pending ED-04.
effect_assessments.fallback: Static end card with the CTA already visible.

effect_assessments.name: light_sweep
effect_assessments.rationale: A sweep adds gloss but does not prove the built-in filter; the real demo is stronger in this film.
effect_assessments.feasibility: Easy in grade or practical lighting.
effect_assessments.limitations: Rejected as decoration for this brief.

effect_assessments.name: particle_glow
effect_assessments.use_case: Add premium sparkle around the product
effect_assessments.rationale: Particles would compete with the pack and imply a quality cue the brand has not asked for.
effect_assessments.rights_safety: No rights issue; disclosure not needed.

effect_assessments.name: cgi_liquid
effect_assessments.use_case: Build a stylised liquid ribbon around the pack
effect_assessments.rationale: CG liquid would add cost and risk an uncanny result; the real pour is more credible and already in the brief.
effect_assessments.rights_safety: No product claim, but simulation needs disclosure if it reads as real evidence.
effect_assessments.limitations: Rejected for cost and credibility on this brief.

synthesis: The product and its core benefit are supported by Blue Tokai's own product and brewing pages: a single-serve sachet with a built-in paper filter, brewed over a 180-200 ml cup with hot water, and a Mixed Bag spanning light to dark roasts. The honest creative route is a visible demo, not an instant-coffee comparison. Price, pack sizes and public product images are observed commercial material and remain rights or approval holds. A real brew includes repeated pours and a two-minute steep, so the film must disclose time compression rather than imply real-time brewing. The range shot needs a real light endpoint, so Seethargundu is added to the supplied Vienna and Attikan packs.
